quests.question: The day ___ we got married was sunny.
quests.hint: We got married ON that day - a hidden preposition again narrows the choice to one pronoun.
quests.explanation: 'When' stands for 'on which' (we got married on that day). 'Where' is wrong because a day is a point in time, not a place.

quests.question: The year ___ I joined the company was difficult.
quests.hint: 'Joined the company' already has its object - the year needs its own hidden preposition.
quests.explanation: Since 'the company' is the object of 'joined', the year connects through a preposition (joined the company IN that year), which 'when' supplies.

quests.question: The morning ___ the exam started felt endless.
quests.hint: The exam started ON that morning - find the pronoun that includes this hidden preposition.
quests.explanation: 'When' replaces 'on which'. Since a morning is a time, not a person, 'who' cannot be the answer.

quests.question: The summer ___ that song came out is unforgettable.
quests.hint: The song came out IN that summer - that hidden preposition guides you to the right pronoun.
quests.explanation: 'When' stands for 'in which' (the song came out in that summer). 'Where' is wrong because a summer is a season, not a location.

quests.question: The moment ___ we landed felt magical.
quests.hint: We landed AT that moment - locate the pronoun built around this preposition.
quests.explanation: 'When' carries the meaning of 'at which'. Since a moment is a point in time, 'who' (a person word) cannot fit.

quests.question: The week ___ I felt sick was right before the trip.
quests.hint: You feel sick DURING a week - the hidden preposition again points to the time pronoun.
quests.explanation: 'When' stands for 'during which'. 'Where' is incorrect because a week refers to time, not a place.

quests.question: The era ___ people relied on letters feels distant now.
quests.hint: 'Relied on letters' already has its object via 'on' - the era needs its own separate hidden preposition.
quests.explanation: Since 'letters' is already the object of 'relied on', the era connects through another preposition (relied on letters DURING that era), which 'when' supplies.

quests.question: The evening ___ the power went out was chaotic.
quests.hint: The power went out ON that evening - find the pronoun that already contains this preposition.
quests.explanation: 'When' replaces 'on which'. 'Why' is wrong because the sentence is describing a time, not giving a reason.

quests.question: The decade ___ smartphones appeared changed everything.
quests.hint: Smartphones appeared IN that decade - that hidden preposition is your clue.
quests.explanation: 'When' stands for 'in which'. A decade refers to time, so the place-word 'where' cannot be correct.

quests.question: The occasion ___ we tried that dish was my birthday.
quests.hint: 'Tried that dish' already has its object - the occasion needs a separate hidden preposition.
quests.explanation: Since 'that dish' is the object of 'tried', the occasion connects through a preposition (tried that dish ON that occasion), which 'when' supplies.

quests.question: The season ___ prices drop is right after the holidays.
quests.hint: Prices drop DURING that season - locate the pronoun containing this hidden preposition.
quests.explanation: 'When' stands for 'during which'. Since a season is a time period, the people-word 'who' cannot be correct here.

quests.question: The semester ___ I studied abroad changed my perspective.
quests.hint: You studied abroad DURING that semester - the hidden preposition guides you to the time pronoun.
quests.explanation: 'When' replaces 'during which'. 'Where' is wrong because a semester names a period of time, not a location.

quests.question: The period ___ my grandparents lived together was full of stories.
quests.hint: They lived together DURING that period - find the pronoun with the hidden preposition built in.
quests.explanation: 'When' stands for 'during which'. Since a period is a stretch of time, the people-word 'who' cannot fit.

quests.question: The night ___ the band played live sold out fast.
quests.hint: The band played live ON that night - that hidden preposition narrows the choice.
quests.explanation: 'When' replaces 'on which'. 'Where' is wrong because a night refers to time, not a physical location.

quests.question: The quarter ___ sales increased surprised the managers.
quests.hint: Sales increased DURING that quarter - locate the time pronoun that fits this hidden preposition.
quests.explanation: 'When' stands for 'during which'. A business quarter is a period of time, so the reason-word 'why' does not fit.

quests.question: The guide ___ we hired spoke five languages.
quests.hint: Hidden clause: 'we hired ___.' A tour guide is a person.
quests.explanation: The guide is the object of 'hired', and since a guide is a person, the object pronoun 'who' is correct.

quests.question: The manager ___ decisions affected the whole team resigned.
quests.hint: 'Decisions' sits right after the gap - that noun signals possession, not action.
quests.explanation: 'Whose decisions' means 'her decisions'. Because a noun follows immediately, the possessive pronoun 'whose' is required.

quests.question: The farm ___ these eggs come from is nearby.
quests.hint: These eggs come FROM the farm - the hidden preposition stretches all the way to the end of the clause.
quests.explanation: 'Where' can stand in for 'from which' even when the preposition is left stranded at the end: 'the farm where these eggs come from'.

quests.question: The rule ___ confuses most students is explained on page ten.
quests.hint: Find the verb right after the gap ('confuses') - that signals a subject pronoun for a thing.
quests.explanation: The rule is the subject of 'confuses'. Since a rule is a thing, 'which' is correct; 'whom' can never act as a subject.

quests.question: The birthday ___ I turned eighteen was unforgettable.
quests.hint: You turn a certain age ON a birthday - that hidden preposition points to the time pronoun.
quests.explanation: 'When' stands for 'on which' (I turned eighteen on that birthday). 'Where' is wrong because a birthday is a date, not a place.

quests.question: This is the catchiest tune ___ I have heard all year.
quests.hint: A superlative ('catchiest') appears again - recall which connector that pattern favors.
quests.explanation: Following the superlative 'the catchiest', natural English favors 'that' over 'which', continuing the pattern from earlier levels.

quests.question: The doctor ___ clinic is downtown specializes in allergies.
quests.hint: 'Clinic' follows the gap directly - a noun in that position always signals possession.
quests.explanation: 'Whose clinic' means 'his clinic'. Because a noun comes right after the gap, only the possessive pronoun 'whose' fits.

quests.question: The kitchen ___ I cook every day needs new tiles.
quests.hint: You cook IN the kitchen - that hidden preposition points to the location pronoun.
quests.explanation: 'Where' replaces 'in which' (I cook in the kitchen every day). Bare 'which' or 'that' would leave the clause without its preposition.

quests.question: The designer ___ I follow online just launched a new line.
quests.hint: Hidden clause: 'I follow ___ online.' A designer here is a person.
quests.explanation: The designer is the object of 'follow', and since the designer is a person, 'who' is the correct pronoun.

quests.question: The gadget ___ I reviewed broke after a week.
quests.hint: Hidden clause: 'I reviewed ___.' A gadget is a thing, not a person.
quests.explanation: The gadget is the object of 'reviewed'. As a thing, it takes 'which', never 'who'.

quests.question: I will always remember the instant ___ I saw her face.
quests.hint: I saw her face AT that instant - the hidden preposition points to the time pronoun.
quests.explanation: 'When' stands for 'at which' (I saw her face at that instant). 'Where' is wrong because an instant is a moment in time, not a place.

quests.question: The airline ___ flights were delayed offered free meals.
quests.hint: 'Flights' sits right after the gap - that noun signals possession, even for a company.
quests.explanation: 'Whose flights' means 'its flights'. Since the airline owns the flights, 'whose' is correct even though an airline isn't a person.

quests.question: The factory ___ these cars are made employs thousands.
quests.hint: These cars are made IN the factory - that hidden preposition points to the location pronoun.
quests.explanation: 'Where' stands for 'in which' (these cars are made in the factory). A factory is not a person, so 'who' is impossible.

quests.question: The relative ___ visits us every Christmas brought a puppy this year.
quests.hint: Find the verb right after the gap ('visits') - that signals a subject pronoun for a person.
quests.explanation: The relative is the subject of 'visits', so 'who' is needed. 'Whom' can never function as a subject, no matter how formal the sentence is.

quests.question: We loved the actors and the scenery ___ made the film unforgettable.
quests.hint: The subject names people (actors) and things (scenery) together - one connector has to cover both.
quests.explanation: Because 'the actors and the scenery' mixes people with things, only 'that' can refer to both at once.
